featured_reviews.review_text: I don't have a sweet tooth but in all honesty, all the sweets I have tried so far from so called "sweet shops" nothing has tasted as yummy & genuine like the ones from Murlidhar. featured_reviews.name: harshad sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely unacceptable experience with Murlidhar Sweets, Borivali. I received a box of sweets that were spoiled and had visible fungus on them. This is not just poor quality — it's a serious health risk. Selling contaminated sweets is dangerous, especially when people trust shops like this during festive occasions.

If this is how they maintain their products, they have no business selling food to the public. It’s clear there’s a complete lack of hygiene, storage standards, and responsibility.

⚠️ A strong warning to everyone: DO NOT buy sweets from Murlidhar during Diwali or any occasion. Don’t risk your family’s health over pretty packaging and false reputation.

Shops like this must be held accountable. I hope the authorities take action before someone falls seriously ill.

Good hospitality turns buying into an experience and make customers try and buy more than too!

featured_reviews.name: Ketan Chothe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located near Lodha Aqua in Mahajanwadi, Mira Road East, Madhuram Sweets appears promising from the outside with a clean and well-maintained shop ambiance. However, the overall experience didn’t meet expectations.

We tried the rasmalai and malai sandwich—unfortunately, both lacked taste and didn’t feel fresh. Given the high pricing, the quality was quite disappointing. For the rate they charge, customers naturally expect better taste and freshness.

Though the shop scores well on cleanliness and presentation, the quality of the products needs serious improvement. Based on our experience with these two items, we didn’t feel confident trying anything else. It’s advisable to check freshness before making a purchase.
